description: Log-periodic spiral-arm fits to the Reid+2019 maser parallaxes. These are fitted model curves, not observations: the observations they are fitted to are the ~200 points in masers.json. There is no photograph of the Milky Way from outside and there never will be.

source.paper: Reid M.J., Menten K.M., Brunthaler A., et al. 2019, ApJ, 885, 131
source.extraText: Sect. 4 (spiral model definition and arm-width gradient) and Sect. 5 ("Updated Spiral Arm Model", per-arm discussion) for the draw ranges and the Carina segment.
source.vizierTable: J/ApJ/885/131 (parallax table; Table 2 itself is not in the VizieR catalogue)

licence: Fitted parameters reproduced from an AAS journal article (ApJ). Cite Reid et al. 2019, ApJ 885, 131. See LICENSE.md in this directory.
attribution: Spiral-arm model: Reid et al. (2019), ApJ 885, 131, Table 2.

model.formulaUnits: R and R_ref in kpc; beta, beta_ref and pitch in RADIANS inside the formula
model.segmentUsage: For each segment, evaluate R(beta) with that segment's betaRefDeg/rRefKpc/pitchDeg over [betaMinDeg, betaMaxDeg]. Segments are chained so R is continuous across boundaries.
model.widthMeaning: The fitted width is the intrinsic 1-sigma width of the distribution of HIGH-MASS STAR-FORMING REGIONS about the arm ridge line. The broader stellar arm is wider than this.
model.toCartesian: X = R * sin(beta), Y = R * cos(beta), Z = 0 (arm ridge line lies in the plane)

frame.name: Galactocentric galactic Cartesian
frame.axes: +X along galactic rotation at the Sun (toward l=90deg); +Y from the Galactic centre toward the Sun; +Z toward the North Galactic Pole. Right-handed; the Galaxy's angular momentum points toward -Z.
frame.betaDefinition: beta = atan2(X, Y): galactocentric azimuth, 0 toward the Sun, increasing in the direction of galactic rotation (Reid+2019 convention).
frame.R0Source: Reid+2019 (8.15 +/- 0.15 kpc). Chosen over GRAVITY Collaboration 2019 (8.178 +/- 0.035 kpc) because the Table 2 arm fits were themselves derived assuming R0 = 8.15 kpc; mixing the two would displace the masers from their own fitted arms.

caveats: betaDataRangeDeg is the azimuth range actually covered by parallax measurements. betaDrawRangeDeg extends past it; extrapolatedBelowDeg / extrapolatedAboveDeg mark where. A renderer should visually de-emphasise the extrapolated portions.

Reid+2019 argue Norma connects to Outer and Scutum-Centaurus connects to OSC. The OSC connection is a direct extension of the same fitted spiral and is drawn. The Norma-Outer join required hand-adjusted pitch angles in the paper and is NOT reproduced here.
Pitch angles for the 3-kpc arm and the inner Norma segment are negative, i.e. those segments wind in the opposite sense. That is what the fit says.

arms.name: 3-kpc arm (near)
arms.drawRangeBasis: Low end set at the galactocentric azimuth of the observed l=337.0 deg tangency (beta=-62.9); high end is the Table 2 data limit + 7 deg.
arms.notes: Associated with the Galactic bar rather than being a true spiral arm (Reid+2019 Sect. 5.5); only 3 parallaxes constrain it.

arms.name: Norma arm
arms.drawRangeBasis: Low end set at the galactocentric azimuth of the observed l=327.5 deg tangency (beta=-42.2); high end is the Table 2 data limit + 6 deg.
arms.notes: Reid+2019 Sect. 5.1 argue the Norma arm most likely wraps around the far side of the Galactic centre and becomes the Outer arm, but their published figure joins the two with hand-adjusted pitch angles. We do NOT extrapolate that join: the two arms are kept as separate fitted segments and the association is recorded in connectsTo only.

arms.name: Scutum-Centaurus-OSC arm
arms.drawRangeBasis: Extended to beta = -230 deg because Reid+2019 Sect. 5.2 state explicitly that extending this same fitted model beyond the Galactic centre carries it back into the 1st quadrant as the Outer Scutum-Centaurus (OSC) arm near R ~ 15 kpc. Beyond beta = -44 deg (the l=306.1 deg tangency) the curve is an extrapolation of the fit, not a fit to data.
arms.notes: Fits exclude six sources near l=30 deg with unusually large proper motions (G030.22-0.17, G030.41-0.23, G030.74-0.04, G030.81-0.05, G030.97-0.14, G031.41+0.30).

arms.name: Sagittarius-Carina arm
arms.drawRangeBasis: High end is the Table 2 data limit + 3 deg. Below beta = -33 deg (the 4th-quadrant tangency quoted in Reid+2019 Sect. 5.3) an extra segment with pitch 10.0 deg is appended, which is the value the authors state they adopt there to match the CO (l,v) trace of the Carina arm.
arms.notes: Two outliers removed from the fit (G032.74-0.07, G033.64-0.22). The kink at beta=24 deg sits in a real 2-kpc-long gap in the arm near (X,Y)=(2,6) kpc.

segments.provenance: Reid+2019 Sect. 5.3 text: "we decrease the pitch angle to 10 deg in order to match the CO (l-v) trace of the Carina arm, assuming kinematic distances".

arms.name: Local arm (Orion spur)
arms.drawRangeBasis: Table 2 data range padded by 6 deg at each end; this is an isolated segment.
arms.notes: A single pitch angle was fitted (psi_< = psi_>). Reid+2019 Sect. 5.5: an isolated arm segment with very significant massive star formation that has not been linked up into a full arm. The Sun sits just inside it (R0 = 8.15 kpc vs R_kink = 8.26 kpc).

arms.name: Perseus arm
arms.drawRangeBasis: Low end is the Table 2 data limit - 7 deg. High end extrapolates the psi_> = 8.7 deg fit inward past the data limit, following Reid+2019 Sect. 5.4 ("extrapolating the arm with this pitch angle inward into the 4th quadrant"). Beyond beta = 115 deg the curve is extrapolation.
arms.notes: Star formation along the arm is markedly uneven: it weakens in the 3rd quadrant and there is an ~8 kpc stretch between l=50 and l=90 deg with little activity.

arms.name: Outer arm
arms.drawRangeBasis: Table 2 data range padded by ~9 deg at each end.
arms.notes: The kink near beta=18 deg rests partly on the revised BeSSeL distance to S269 of 4.15 +/- 0.22 kpc (Quiroga-Nunez+2019), which favours Asaki+2014 over Honma+2007.
